doc: Home's board: the merge of Nearby and Favourites. Three exclusive sections — `catch` (saved, and still makeable), `saved` (the rest of the rider's list at any distance, soonest first) and `nearby` (what is around them, nearest first, minus anything already above). One card shape throughout: a place, the routes the rider saved there with readings, then every OTHER route there as a chip with none. The ranking in one line: SAVED OUTRANKS NEAR, DUE-SOON OUTRANKS FAR. `catch` needs a position and a live figure; without either there is no band and the row stays where it is, because a rider must never be shown a bus they were told they would catch and cannot.

homeView.doc: The whole board in one call.

cases.why: The wire gap, pinned so it cannot change silently: `/v1/nearby` sends readings and a routeCount but no route list, so a nearby card's chips are the lines among its readings and `chipsMore` is everything else. cases.name: the-band-is-tight-when-the-walk-nearly-eats-the-arrival
cases.why: `catch` is the arrival minus the walk, banded rather than printed. From 320 m (a 4-minute walk) a bus 5 minutes out leaves one minute of slack and is `tight`; one 12 minutes out is `comfortable`; and a board with no arrival has no figure to subtract from, so it has no band at all.

cases.name: a-place-with-only-a-timetable-sorts-below-one-with-a-bus-and-above-one-with-nothing
cases.why: The three tiers, one level up. A card is ranked by its own soonest row, so a place whose operator publishes no route-level feed (Citybus, GMB) reads its frequency and sits below every place with a sighting — and a place whose board says nothing at all sits below that. Ordering cards by anything other than their rows would let a card claim a position its contents do not support.

cases.name: a-saved-key-that-no-longer-resolves-still-draws-its-place
cases.why: A favourite naming a route the place no longer serves — a renumbered line, a retired variant. The card stays, with no rows and the place's routes as chips: dropping it would make a rider's hand-curated list silently shrink, and the key may resolve again on the next dataset build. It sorts last, because it has nothing to be sooner than.

cases.why: `getStop` promotes a member pole to its place, so two saved poles of one interchange resolve to the SAME place and arrive twice. One card, because a rider who saved two lines at two kerbs of one place saved two things at one place — `favouritesView`'s rule, and Home inherits it rather than re-deciding it.

cases.name: a-line-boarding-at-two-kerbs-is-one-chip
cases.why: Since WP5-9 the wire sends one reading per line PER BOARDING POLE, so a line at two kerbs of a place arrives twice. A chip strip carries no kerb, so two identical badges would ask a rider to choose between them and give them nothing to choose with — the same collapse `stopCardView` makes for a card with no per-kerb heading. It also keeps `chipsMore` honest: one unit on both sides of the subtraction.

cases.why: `parseRouteId` returns nothing for an id the grammar does not cover, and the chip falls back to the whole id — the same fallback `stopCardView` makes, and for the same reason: an unreadable id should still show the rider something rather than an empty badge.

cases.name: a-bus-at-the-kerb-sorts-above-a-place-whose-keys-no-longer-resolve
cases.why: Two tiers the comparator only reaches with more than one card: a reading already inside `dueUnderSec` reads Due and sorts first, and a place whose saved keys resolve to nothing has no row to be sooner than and sorts last. A one-card section never calls the comparator, so both of these were unmeasured until this row.
